- When sentiment is positive (≥0.5) and forecast is flat or rising slowly, model tends to underpredict sharp upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 2–5% for the next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.3) and forecast is rising, model often overestimates recovery; cap upward slope at 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 3–8% for next 5–10 days if sentiment remains neutral or negative.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from +0.7 to -0.3 within 3 days), model often lags; shift forecast downward by 1–3% per day for 3–5 days after sentiment turn.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is consistently 5–10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes or price diverges.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period volatility; add 1–3% buffer to forecast if sentiment is volatile or recent price action shows high variance.
